content.label: You can't have a notes app across all devices without having a version either on web or on windows. Massive oversight. Until fixed, I'll be sticking with notion.
Updated app automatically and changed formatting on some of my notes. No longer trust these people. They have changed some of the basic styling on the app in the name of so called improvements.
I wanted a notes app that was MacBook friendly and bear does just that. Love how clean the app is also!
I use Bear daily to maintain project notes and todos. I love it. If I had one feature request it would be to allow switching between different profiles e.g. Work & Personal.

I’ve used Bear for years, as a replacement for OneNote and Evernote. It took a long time to get to version 2, but it’s so worth it. Everything I was looking for, nothing lost from version 1. Very fast, love the tagging system, and so much more flexible than other note taking apps
Simply the best.

title.label: I would give bear 5 stars but..

content.label:
Bear is one of the most used productivity apps on my phone. Has everything I would want from a note taking app and its simple to use. 

Its smooth to use and has a lot of more complicated functions that you dont need be if used can make your experience even better. 

I personally love the way notes can be categorised.  

My only gripe with them is (although it’s been in the works for the last how many years) there is no way for me to bring my notes over/ontop my PC. It can be a little annoying when working on your PC and not being able to drag and drop info into one place. 

Thats why I gave it 4/5 for an app that really deserves 5/5.

I was looking for a way to record my voice on the watch and have it save as a note which then syncs to all my devices, Bear has that covered. I also love the browser extensions that allow for you to save a webpage as a note, very handy for saving recipes and ingredient list to view on the watch while at the shops. Looking forward to the web version so I can access my notes from any device.

title.label: V2 an improvement on a great app

content.label:
I use Bear for collecting recipes (of which I have 000’s) and it’s been a great app. Have used V2 for a few days and lots of improvements making it more if a pleasure to use. 
Would like to be able to have a facility to keep recipes in a separate folder then use it for other or install 2 Bears (yes I know I can tag etc, but want a completely separate facility). 
Anyway, highly recommend both versions of Bear.

I’ve been using bear for around 4 years now. I pay for the monthly subscription so I can use on both my phone and Mac. As a writer, student, and chronic planner, I use bear for everything, throughout my entire day. I’ve made about 2500 notes by this point over the years; there’s just something about the app which I’ve come to accustomed to that I struggle to write in other mediums now. 

There is only one thing I would suggest, which would be to be able to add in grids as sometimes when I’m doing daily schedules or meal plans I feel like that feature that is something that’s missing, but apart from that, it’s my favourite app and I would HIGHLY recommend.
This is what note taking should be - easy, intuitive, functionally rich enough. There’s a lot of DESIGN THINKING that has gone into this app. Buy the Pro version. Well done Bear people!

This app is great for storing notes and by far the best app out there. I enjoy the privacy as well as the different features it offers such as storing photos in the notes section.

2 things which would make this app perfect:

1: when you add a photo into the note, you can’t add privacy on to the note and hide it. 

2: a undo option would be great. When accidentally deleting text there’s no undo button or option.

Other than that the app is great.

I’ve been using Bear for about 4 years now. The one thing I love about it the most is it’s not forever trying to change and be something new. It’s almost looked exactly the same in all the time I’ve used it and that’s a great feature. The subscription cost is also excellent value.
Best note app!

title.label: No different than Apple’s own Notes app

content.label: Yet, it’s not free, furthermore - not available to actually buy. Subscriptions everywhere… yawn. Delete.

iCloud sync is locked behind a subscription fee 🤢

Wonderful to use, well designed, themed etc. but I don’t like blocking of essential functionality behind a subscription fee. Especially considering iCloud sync comes with my phone already… why am I paying to unlock a feature that already comes with my iPhone. 

I’d have the subscription for encryption and themes - collaborative notes etc.  but not for something as basic and essential as iCloud syncing. This is basic functionality imo.
Fast and efficient, note app with great simple features and nice aesthetically pleasingly
I liked everything about this app until I realised how awful the quality of images are in notes. It's just impossible to read texts!

Nuff said?

Wiki features! Tagging … markup… exports … all devices. Love it. 

Generally hate subscriptions but these guys have a product that has earned my respect and I am completely happy to sub. 

I have been using the app continuously since Feb 2019 for my at work professional daily log and tech notes (hello wiki).

title.label: Meh, not a bad app! Two missing stars for a reason.

content.label: Ok this is an average app, there is nothing bad with it However, there is nothing that stands out to make it anything special. It’s a little shy on features to warrant a subscription. I wanted to try Bear but more out of curiosity than a requirement. I tried Ulysses awhile back and they share similarities under the hood. One similarity is that you need to export files and can’t seem to access them on your drive (I’ve not spent much time trying). I have my Markdown apps of choice but I noticed a free trial period and thought I’d give it a go. However, the free trial didn’t happen and I was immediately charged for a full year. Now, it is a good app, it’s aesthetics are as most people report; beautiful. Eye candy aside, it works well and does what it says on the tin. The elusive two stars from my review are of course due to the charge. I took a screen shot to prove that I was offered a free trial. In all honesty this happened with another app on the same day. Therefore, the problem may be with the App Store. I’d buy this app for a one off fee at around £20 but I’d want direct access to my files. After moving away from Ulysses demonstrated to me the reason why this binding of users files is practiced in subscription apps I’m far more careful. Developers know it’s a flawed model after all and we all got to eat I suppose. 🙄

title.label: The Best App in the World

content.label: Seriously, it’s the best app in the world. What else is there to say? Thanks Bear.

title.label: Good things come to those who wait

content.label: An excellent app. I have enjoyed using it for the past three years.  Unfortunately, other apps like Apple Notes are slowly creeping up behind with some of the necessary tools I need to make notes which are not a subscription. I am in the process of thinking of cancelling my subscription as over the last couple of years; the improvement has been prolonged. I have seen some excellent features in Panda. Still, patience is running thin in terms of the amount of money which is not a lot, and the time you have to wait, which is a lot. I will see how things proceed over the next few months. I would’ve given it a five star if you could use it via the web. I know it’s a small team and quality over quantity is something I see they are looking into hence my patience. I would recommend this app to anyone, but as I said, Apple Notes are creeping up quite quickly, and I am finding it hard to decide why I should pay for a subscription where the development is prolonged. Let’s see what happens.

title.label: Why I love to write with Bear

content.label: I cannot think of anywhere, I’d rather write my rhymes than Bear, its stylish looks and nifty features, make Bear the best of all the creatures, It lets me write distraction-free, while I type my way through mugs of tea, from “eureka I’ve got it“ to puzzled frown, I jot my thoughts down in Markdown, every detail designed with care, that’s why I love to write with Bear.

I don’t normally leave reviews but I need to on this app. So, expect an honest review below. First of all, this is literally the best app on my phone. I’m using this to write a book. Evernote and the ordinary iPhone notes app cannot compete! This is because it is so aesthetically pleasing to the eye. There are three themes to choose from: white background with black text and red highlights, white background with black text and blue highlights, but I use the black background with white text and blue highlights. I also use this notes app not only for my book, but for making lists and planning. It has a lot of uses! Second of all, the layout is perfect on all devices. I have this app installed on my iPhone and iPad and the app makes it user-friendly. When you first open the app, you’ll see a note already made. It is basically a tutorial. The app is very simple to use and navigate, which helps it’s amazing layout. There is nothing wrong with this app. I have zero problems and suggestions. Kind regards, @tsundoqku on Instagram and Wattpad.
Best writing app there is. Been there for me for years. Couldn’t live without it. Forget the rest. Go with Bear.

title.label: Great app but needs better handwriting support

content.label: The app is great and I've been using it for a while but it really lacks in good handwriting support compared to other apps.

title.label: Great Markdown text and to do app

content.label: Elegant, functional and beautifully thought through text, to do and Markdown text editor. A real no-brainer to elect for the pro subscription.

I really love Bear.  I use it to collect and organise photos of my ceramics work and it’s pretty perfect. The tags allow me to keep track of my experiments and results. I was slightly frustrated that I couldn’t search for multiple tags at once, but then I looked at the help and it turned out that I could, I just hadn’t investigated. The search functions are actually impressively sophisticated and easy to learn to use if you read the help. 

I do think it’s a shame that the app is subscription based. I’d be happy to pay a one off fee to support the development but I’m not prepared to pay a subscription. I do worry that the free version (which actually offers all that I need) will not remain free long term as I’d be surprised if enough people pay for the app just to synch. Fingers crossed as it’s by far the most useful free app that I have.

title.label: Brilliant alternative for a multi-os world

content.label: I like apple notes. It just works. But when you’re trying to jump onto another OS it’s not so great. That’s where Bear comes in. The formatting and layout is gorgeous, it’s very intelligent and it syncs across all platforms and devices. The yearly subscription is a bargain in my opinion, it even comes with a months free trial.
A clean, extensive Notes app with none of the fuss if others. Syncs perfectly, UI is a delight. Would absolutely recommend. Can't do without it.

title.label: Great but not a fan of subscription

content.label:
Really great app but either the subscription cost would need to be lower or a lifetime purchase option available for me to switch.  I decided to go with Spaces instead because of their lifetime purchase option. Spaces appears to be about a year behind Bear in its development but it’s being updated very frequently so I’m ok with that. 

Like I said, this is a really great app and if you are ok with the cost (everyone has a different view on price/value) then don’t hesitate to purchase it, you won’t be disappointed!
I think Bear does more than Apple notes! I like it so much! I suggest 1 thing to be added. Dark mode for uses to choose the themer

title.label: It’s probably the best productivity app you will buy…

content.label:
I’m always on the search for the ultimate productivity tool. It’s a competitive sector and many ultimately disappoint. I tried Bear when it first came out, then left it. Recently I’ve returned and realised that Bear is that ultimate tool.
The combination of Markdown, iCloud sync and one payment across all platforms, allied to a beautiful interface and presentation of your work and ease of use makes this one of the most useful apps you can buy.
I’m not a big fan of subscription services but the price of the Pro subscription for all that flexibility does make it worthwhile.
I’ve just taken on a small admin job along side my normal work. It came with a cheap, plastic PC laptop and years of MS Word files and no particular organisation. I’ve started to use Bear to make some sense out of the chaos and move from Word to Markdown as the default format, exporting to PDF for documents which need to be seen externally. Putting one of the original Word documents side by side with the equivalent Bear version almost makes me laugh. How  much of the world of work can put up with such archaic ugliness. Bear stands head and shoulders above. Brilliant app and lots more potential to come, I’m sure.
is the best “note” app that i found, i use for everything thing, keep documents, memory’s and contacts, just really miss the opinion for create folders... is that ask to much???

Opened app to be faced with that utterly brain dead very light grey text on white. Could have been worse and way more coooool if Red on black or numb nut green on purple. Why this cretinous form of comms is so prevalent is way beyond my intellectual pay grade. So I continue passing my IPad to those with X-ray standard vision and asking them “What the F..k does this say

Honestly, I doubted this app at first but I was wrong. It really helps me and I really don’t write reviews because pretty much all of the apps I downloaded are not great. Thanks to this app I can happily write not paying. I encourage you to use this app it’s wonderful for writing a long text or maybe even a story. DOWNLOAD IT PLS IT WILL HELP YOU ! Just joking you don’t have too BUT IT WILL HELP YOU 😃
Does what it promises and does it exceptionally well.

title.label: Favourite but needs to have a more compact view.

content.label: I love this app so much but the only thing I really don’t like about it is that it looks a bit messy with all the notes on the side showing large thumbnails with headings and pictures. I wish it could just be the title of the page. I don’t know why there is no option for a more compact view. Also, a toggle option like there is in Notion or Obsidian would be really good as well. Because the notes can be quite long sometimes. Other than that, I love this app.

Lack of Windows version or even a WebApp in 2021 is “a bit” disappointing. I had a sub for more than a year but I was tired of not having the access to my text from many devices. So I moved to the other app. There is also Typora an amazing markdown editor for both Mac and Windows. 
There is a problem with notes sorting too. As the only option is to use tags. It’s not the best to say at least. 
Other than that app is solid.

个人感觉最好用的markdown文本软件之一。从初级到深度用户的支持都非常棒。此外希望有没有可能日后加入一个针对笔记的批注功能？因为在重新读笔记的时候可能会有新的思考，虽然可以重新开一篇然后link到原笔记，但是如果能直接在原文上进行批注，可能对思路的展现的效果会更加直观。
祝好！

A beautiful text editor made available at a very reasonable cost. Missing some rather basic features, such as Folders, which is still my preference over nested tags. 

Development, however, is glacial, with no major updates to the editor in the current year. “Panda”, version 2.0 of the text editor engine is still currently in Alpha, with no indication of release date.

This is so close to being perfect — support for node view (like Obsidian) would make this perfect.

Somewhere in the past 6 months the Bear version that ‘was free’ was downgraded as the new Pro subscriptions were introduced, this seems to have meant that syncing no longer worked for the original free patrons, I’m don’t know if this is what has happened, but after an update I have lost important pieces of writing that cannot be restored as they were seemingly never saved, I’m horrified to discover this, I relied on Bear as a peaceful simplistic app for creative writing, and am hugely disappointed at the loss of my work, I have read other reviews about this so please please beware.

title.label: MAKE A GO BACK FEATURE PLEASEEE

content.label: MAKE A GO BACK FEATURE PLEASEEE
New to this app usually use Evernote but needed a new app to work with, looks works and feels really well so already join bear pro!

title.label: The best notes app. On any platform

content.label:
I love Bear.

Clean, simple design, notes are quickly created and edited, and easily grouped and categorised. Search is powerful and editing tools are rich and full featured and features for sharing and sending notes are all where you need them and they just work. 

Companion apps for MacOS and Apple Watch (importantly at no extra cost) just seamlessly work. I love being able to update a note in my phone or Mac and then later pull it up on my Watch, this is what cross-platform applications should look like. 

I use it every day, and it does exactly what I need. Brilliant.
Love this app, so clean and easy to use.

title.label: Far and away the best notebook app

content.label:
I’ve been looking for the best digital notebook for years. Finally I’ve found it in Bear. 

I keep my work notes, my personal notes and everything else in it. The themes are gorgeous and the simplicity is perfectly weight with the features I want. 

I use it everyday.

I’m absolutely awful at organising. With Bear whatever you type you can search for at the top. Typed some random quote from 5 months ago? Write it into the search bar and it finds the document for you, has literally saved me so much time and effort. If you are a lazy uni student like myself, you need to use this app. So useful.
This is the only app that keeps me using iOS.

Bear has a lovely interface and lots of great features. I love the fact you can easily insert files including by copy and pasting, there are multiple export options and you can add multiple nested tags. I also love the fact you can share to existing or new notes, including the option to insert a titled link which I use all the time. Brilliant and well worth the very low asking price for Pro.
